newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH POLITICAL AGENDA FOR SEPTEMBER 30-OCTOBER 4.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH POLITICAL AGENDA FOR SEPTEMBER 30-OCTOBER 4.

text.p: - Following are some of
the main issues scheduled for debate in the Dutch parliament
this week:
MEDICINES -- Criteria for pharmaceuticals to be admitted to
list of medicines required to be covered by insurers will be
debated on Wednesday. Health Minister tightened admission rules
in July 1993, saving at least 540 million guilders on health
care budget.
LOBBYING -- Debate on setting limits to private lobbying by
MPs expected to be called for by Labour Party on Tuesday. Debate
follows revelations last week on right liberal party leader's
personal intervention with Health Minister over Merck Sharp &
Dohme, a pharmaceutical company of which the MP a supervisory
board member.
SOIL POLLUTION -- MPs on Thursday debate proposal to
financially support companies responsible for cleaning up
polluted soil. Subsidy will be paid in case clean-up operation
costs exceed 10 million guilders.
Other debates:-
TUESDAY:
- Allocating permits to oil companies for building petrol
stations.
- Relaxation of judicial rules to reduce acquittals on
technical grounds such as misspelled address.
WEDNESDAY:
- Debate on powers of special task force which is to develop
instruments to sustain Dutch export industry.
- Establishing new advisory council to Transport Minister.
- Ecological farmers will plead MPs to support measures
strengthening position of environmentally sound agriculture.
- Cleaning up polluted sediments in rivers and lakes.
THURSDAY:
- Debate on controversial proposal to exclude illegal
immigrants from social services will be resumed.
FRIDAY:
- MPs will take the high speed train to Paris to assess its
qualities in anticipation of debate on controversial plans to
build high speed train track between Amsterdam and Brussels.
The Lower House last week discussed:
TAX EXEMPTION -- Majority approved legislation exempting
market gardening sector from paying social charges for seasonal
workers.
BOUTROS-GHALI -- Foreign Minister said Netherlands will not
support second term for UN-secretary-general Boutros Boutros-
Ghali.
INSIDER TRADING -- Council of State urged Finance Secretary
to reconsider proposal to tighten up legislation against insider
trading. Advise could bring MPs to amend and moderate new and
stricter legislation.
